(7 goals) | total goals = | average goals = | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2006 Thailand Premier League|2006]] | nextseason = [[2008 Thailand Premier League|2008]] }} The '''2007 [[Thai Premier League]]''' had 16 teams, combining the 12 member clubs from the [[Thai Premier League 2006|2006 season]], the top two clubs from [[Thailand Division 1 League|Division 1]], and two clubs from the [[Provincial League|Pro League]] 1. The official name of the league at this time was '''Thailand Premier League'''. Matches were normally played on Saturdays with a 4pm kick off time but there were some 5pm or 6pm started and some midweek fixtures. Evening kick offs were rare. The season would have a three-month break from mid-May to mid-August because of the Asian Cup which was being co-hosted by [[Thailand]] from July 7–29 and the world university games, the [[2007 Summer Universiade|Universiade]], in [[Bangkok]] from August 8–18. Normally only the Premier League champions are allowed to take part in the [[AFC Champions League]]. However, for the 2007 season, the runners-up would also be admitted due to the late completion of [[Indonesia]]n domestic [[Liga Indonesia|league]] and [[Piala Indonesia|cup]] competitions. ==Member Songkhram FC|Samut Songkhram]] * Thai Premier League was combined with [[Provincial League]] completely. [[Chonburi FC]] was the first club from Provincial League that was the champion of Thai Premier League in this season. ==Asian representation== *League champions [[Bangkok University FC|Bangkok University]] took centre stage for Thailand in their first foray into the [[2007 AFC Champions League|Asian Champions League]], they put up a good fight, losing 3 games and drawing 3 games in an impressive campaign, although they still finished bottom of their group stage. Only one team would be for the [[Asian Champions League]] due to the fact that Australia entered the Asian Confederation. *[[Osotsapa FC|Osotsapa]] would enter the [[2007 AFC Cup]], the first time a Thai team would enter this competition. They came third in their group, and only 3 points behind the group winners. * After reaching the final the previous year, [[Chonburi F.C.|Chonburi]] made a swift exit from the [[Singapore Cup]] getting beat in the first round by [[Balestier Khalsa FC|Balestier Khalsa]]. [[Bangkok University FC|Bangkok University]] brought back some pride when they duly dispatched of [[Balestier Khalsa FC|Balestier Khalsa]] in the Quarter-Final stage before being knocked out by
